'''Sovereign Gold Bond''', abbreviated as SGB, is a government security issued by the [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI) on behalf of the [[Government of India]]. It is denominated in grams of [[gold]] and is linked to the price of gold in [[India]]. It is also an interest-bearing bond, carrying an [[interest]] of 2.5% {{Abbr|p.a.|per annum}} paid in two installments every year till maturity.

The bond has an 8-year term with an option for early withdrawal through the RBI after 5 years. It is listed and traded on Indian stock exchanges, allowing eligible investors to buy or sell anytime through their [[Dematerialization (securities)|demat]] accounts. It can also be transferred to other eligible investors without redemption through the RBI.

The scheme was discontinued in 2024 due to being an expensive method of borrowing for the government. Existing bonds were not affected.

== History ==
The scheme was initially announced in the [[2015 Union budget of India|2015 Union budget]]. It was approved by the [[Union Council of Ministers|cabinet]] on 9 September 2015, and was launched by [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] in an event in [[New Delhi]] on 5 November 2015. The event was also attended by the [[Finance minister of india|Union Minister for Finance]] [[Arun Jaitley]], the Minister of State for Finance [[Jayant Sinha]] and the Minister of State for [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|Commerce & Industry]] [[Nirmala Sitharaman]]. == Eligibility ==

People residing in India, as defined in the [[Foreign Exchange Management Act|Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999]] are eligible to invest in SGBs. These include individuals, [[Hindu joint family|Hindu Undivided Families]] (HUFs),  [[University|universities]], [[Trust (law)|trusts]], and [[Charitable organization|charitable institutions]]. People who become non-residents after buying an SGB can still hold it until maturity or premature redemption.

The bonds are issued in 1-gram denominations and multiples thereof. Each eligible investor can purchase up to 4 kg per financial year. A demat account is optional; bonds can be held in dematerialized form with a securities depository or tracked by the RBI.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=2019-02-04 |title=Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme |url=https://www.rbi.org.in/commonperson/English/Scripts/FAQs.aspx?Id=1658 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409140146/https://www.rbi.org.in/commonperson/english/scripts/FAQs.aspx?Id=1658 |archive-date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=[[Reserve Bank of India]]}} </ref>

== Price ==
The issue price is the average closing price of 999 purity gold from the last 3 business days before the subscription period, as published by the India Bullion and Jewelers Association Limited (IBJA). The redemption price, for both early and maturity redemptions, is the average closing price from the 3 business days before repayment.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kulkarni |first=Sneha |date=2024-02-15 |title=New Sovereign Gold Bond tranche: Is SGB Series IV 2023-24 issue price highest ever offered? |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/invest/new-sovereign-gold-bond-tranche-is-sgb-series-iv-2023-24-issue-price-highest-ever-offered/articleshow/107649033.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224165615/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/invest/new-sovereign-gold-bond-tranche-is-sgb-series-iv-2023-24-issue-price-highest-ever-offered/articleshow/107649033.cms |archive-date=2024-02-24 |access-date=2024-04-25 |work=[[The Economic Times]] |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

Sovereign Gold Bond, abbreviated as SGB, is a government security issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Government of India. It is denominated in grams of gold and is linked to the price of gold in India. It is also an interest-bearing bond, carrying an interest of 2.5% p.a. paid in two installments every year till maturity.
The bond has an 8-year term with an option for early withdrawal through the RBI after 5 years. It is listed and traded on Indian stock exchanges, allowing eligible investors to buy or sell anytime through their demat accounts. It can also be transferred to other eligible investors without redemption through the RBI.
The scheme was discontinued in 2024 due to being an expensive method of borrowing for the government. Existing bonds were not affected.
